question.text: An investor compares real estate investment with REITs. Which of the following is an advantage of REITs over direct real estate?

answer.text: REITs offer higher rental yields than direct property ownership
REITs have no market risk as they invest in physical properties
REITs are listed on exchanges, offer better liquidity, and provide diversification across multiple commercial properties
REITs allow the investor to choose which specific properties to invest in

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B, direct real estate is a large, concentrated and illiquid exposure, whereas REIT exposure is spread over many commercial properties, is run by a professional investment manager, may be listed on an exchange, and offers relatively better liquidity. These attributes together make listed REITs an advantage over direct property for an investor seeking diversified commercial real estate exposure. The Trap: REITs do carry market risk because their listed units fluctuate in price, and individual unit holders cannot choose which specific properties the REIT holds; allocation decisions are made by the investment manager. Options claiming "no market risk" or property-level choice misread how a listed REIT works. Note: The source page supports the qualitative liquidity and diversification advantages but does not specify a minimum direct-property ticket size or detailed volatility drivers, so the answer is anchored to the source comparison rather than to any specific entry-price figure.
